interactables.text: The Gardener, [Basil], is trimming a hedge that has nothing left to give. 'Oh good,' he tells it, not looking up. 'A cat. Cats are natural. Cats belong outside. Like ALL animals.' Snip. Snip.

topics.prompt: Watch his hands while he trims
topics.text: The shears wobble mid-snip. 'Animals belong in [Nature],' he announces - to the hedge, to the fountain, to the concept of justice. 'A cage is a prison with better catering.' He glances at the mansion. 'Not that I would DO anything about it. That would be wrong. Probably.'

'The mud? BULBS. I was planting bulbs.' He holds up the [mud-caked gloves] as evidence, realizes evidence is exactly the problem, and puts them behind his back. 'Daffodils. For spring. Ask the flower bed.' The flower bed, freshly turned, backs him up.

topics.prompt: Sit between him and the bent shears. Wait.
topics.text: The snipping stops. The fountain burbles. Somewhere, a gull. You wait the way only a cat can wait.|'ALRIGHT. FINE. [I opened the cage]. Me, with the shears, just before six - everyone was fussing over dinner.' It falls out of him like loose soil. 'But he stayed RIGHT HERE. Splashing in his bath, yelling his little phrases, happy as spring. I would never take him AWAY. Away from a garden? That is just a smaller cage, cat.'

interactables.text: Heavy iron [Pruning Shears] left near the fountain. The blade tips are [slightly bent] - the kind of bend you'd get forcing a metal latch.
A stone bird bath near the hedgerow. A few [bright feathers] float on the surface - Rudebeak's distinctive markings. Still crisp, not waterlogged. He was here [this evening].
